desc:
The range of a subtree is its largest value minus its smallest value. The subtree of a node consists of the node and all of its descendants, so a leaf has range 0.

Return the sum of the ranges of the subtrees of all nodes of the tree.

How trees are given. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level order (top to bottom, left to right). The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn; a missing child is written as -1 (real node values are never negative). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped.

For example, [1,2,3,-1,4] is the tree whose root 1 has children 2 and 3; node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child; node 3 is a leaf.

Example 1

tree = [4,8,5,0,1,-1,6]
Output: 17
Ranges: root 8 - 0 = 8; node 8: 8 - 0 = 8; node 5: 6 - 5 = 1; the leaves 0, 1 and 6: 0 each.

Example 2

tree = [1,2,3]
Output: 2
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly
hints: Recomputing the maximum and minimum of every subtree from scratch is quadratic on a chain. Reuse the answers of the children.
The maximum of a subtree is the largest of the node's value and the maxima of its two child subtrees; the minimum works the same way.
Sweep the level-order array from the last index to 0, keep mx[u] and mn[u], and add mx[u] - mn[u] to the total at every node.
editorial: For node u, mx[u] = max(val[u], mx[l], mx[r]) and mn[u] = min(val[u], mn[l], mn[r]), where missing children are ignored. The range of the subtree of u is mx[u] - mn[u]; adding it up over all nodes gives the answer.

Because each child has a larger level-order index than its parent, one backwards sweep finishes the children before their parent. Time O(n), memory O(n). The total is at most 3,000 * 100,000 = 3 * 10<sup>8</sup>, so it fits in 32 bits.
